On the other hand, the pre-emptee-purchaser contested the suit by filing written objection denying the pre-emptor's case and stated that the pre-emptee-purchaser pur-chased the case property with the knowledge of the pre-emptor. The pre-emptee-purchaser developed the case property by raising wall and filling earth on the case property and spent Taka 2,00,000 in raising 132 feet wall and Taka 1,00,000 in filling earth. The pre-emptee developed the case land by spending huge amount of money. The pre-emptor had knowledge at the time of giving possession of the case property The pre-emptee-purchaser by mutating the case property opened Khatian No.4161 in his name and paid off rent regularly. The preemptor with false claim filed the instant suit. Accordingly, he prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 15. He finally submits that the trial Court on proper consideration of the settled principle of law arrived at a right findings that in a case of pre-emption under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, if a tenant is co-sharer in the plot he is also treated as a co-sharer in that plot even if the said plot is recorded in more than one khatian. In support of his submissions, he referred two decisions, reported in 65 DLR (AD) 82 and 7 ADC 603. Accordingly, he prayed for dismissing the Appeal and discharging the Rule. 

 "In a case of pre-emption filed under section 24 of the Act if a co-sharer tenant owns a portion of land in any plot, he is to be treated as co-sharer in the entire plot even if the land of that plot is recorded in more than one khatian. In the event of transfer of a portion of land of that plot appertaining to another khatian a co-sharer tenant can filed a pre-emption case under section 24 of the Act notwithstanding the fact that he does not have any interest in that khatian."
